newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Somaliland appeals for aid to counter drought.
newsitem.headline: Somaliland appeals for aid to counter drought.

text.p: Somaliland, the self-declared republic that split from Somalia in 1991, appealed on Sunday for urgent assistance to counter drought affecting large areas of the Horn of Africa.
Neighbouring Ethiopia and Somalia, and nearby Kenya are all affected by the latest drought, which aid workers say is already raising fears of famine.
Officials in Hargeisa said many wells and boreholes were dry and others were running out of water. Pastureland had been devastated and former grazing areas are now deserted.
In many areas the price of a barrel of water has risen more than seven times and is beyond the reach of many nomadic herdsmen whose cattle and goats are dying in large numbers, they said.
The Somaliland Drought Relief Committee held meetings last week with representatives of U.N. and other aid organisations.
Majdi Dawabi, operations officer of the U.N. children's fund, UNICEF, said after the meetings: "The drought is occurring on an almost annual basis. We need to find a long-term solution."

Somaliland, which has not been recognised by other states, covers the area of the former British Somaliland, which joined its southern neighbour Italian Somalia to form the independent Republic of Somalia in 1960.
